name: Krippenmuseum Wildermieming
kurzbeschreibung: The Krippenmuseum in Wildermieming on the sunny plateau: over 50 artistic Tyrolean and oriental nativity scenes by master woodcarvers.
beschreibung:
Overview

The atmospheric Krippenmuseum Wildermieming is located on the sun-drenched Mieminger Plateau in the municipality of Wildermieming (Innsbruck-Land district) at an elevation of around 870 metres. Set against a picturesque backdrop at the foot of the mighty Mieminger Kette and the Hohe Munde, this museum is an acclaimed cultural institution celebrating authentic Tyrolean folk devotion. Displaying more than 50 masterfully crafted nativity scenes, the museum documents the centuries-old Tyrolean nativity carving and Lenten crib tradition, officially recognized by UNESCO as intangible cultural heritage.

Nativity Art & Masterpieces

The exhibition was brought to life through the dedicated work of the Krippenverein Wildermieming, which preserves both historical and contemporary masterpieces by regional woodcarvers and crib makers. During a stroll through the atmospheric, softly lit exhibition rooms, visitors experience the full spectrum of alpine and oriental nativity art: on display are intricate Tiroler Heimatkrippen, which transplant the biblical Christmas narrative into snow-covered alpine landscapes framed by historic Tyrolean farmhouses and alpine chalets, as well as monumental oriental display cribs featuring detailed caravanserais, bazaars, and desert oases. Hand-carved wooden figurines by renowned Tyrolean carver dynasties are clothed in hand-woven, fine brocade and silk fabrics. A rare cultural and historical highlight are the Fasten- und Passionskrippen (Lenten and Passion cribs), which portray the Passion and Resurrection of Christ in deeply moving scenes. Numerous showcases illustrate the delicate, multi-step crafting process – from preliminary sketches and wood sculpting to polychrome painting and miniature plaster and timber stonework.

Visit & Getting There

The Krippenmuseum Wildermieming is open during the pre-Christmas and winter season from late November to late January on Saturdays and Sundays from 14:00 to 17:00; during the summer months, guided tours for groups of 8 or more are available at any time upon advance reservation. Admission prices (as of the 2025/2026 season): adults approx. €5.00, seniors approx. €4.00, children and youths (aged 6 to 15) approx. €2.50, toddlers free; family ticket approx. €12.00. Visitors holding the regional Welcome Card of the Innsbruck region enjoy discounted admission. Getting there by car: via the Inntalautobahn A12 (exit Telfs West), continue along Mieminger Straße B189 up to the sunny plateau and into Wildermieming; free parking is available at the Gemeindeamt/Vereinshaus. By public transport: take ÖBB trains to Bahnhof Telfs-Pfaffenhofen, then board Postbus line 4176 directly to the stop Wildermieming Gemeindeamt.

Tips

The museum located inside the Vereinshaus offers step-free accessibility and is easily reached by wheelchair users and pushchairs via an access ramp and threshold-free doors. After visiting the museum, enjoy a walk along the Bergdoktorhaus-Weg to the historic inn that served as the filming backdrop for the popular television series. Warm up at the nearby village café with hot spiced cider (Apfelglühmost) and homemade Tyrolean Zelten fruit bread.
